# Results for the proposal

**Generated by `python -m shahid.make_docs` from result files. Do not edit by hand.** Sources: `results/cp7_heldout.json`, `results/cp10.json`, `results/cp10_world.json`, `results/iforest.json`, `results/cp11_select.json`, `results/cp11_eval.json`, `results/cp12.json`, `results/audit.json`. Ledger: `docs/CLAIMS_LEDGER.md`. All data is simulated (`docs/LIMITATIONS.md`).

Reporting rules: never quote accuracy-when-deciding without coverage; quote headline rates as the range over the three evaluations (§0); labelled-episode precision comes from an artificial mix of about one event per day and is not field precision; nominal figures depend on the uncalibrated diversity parameter. Rounding rule: an estimate keeps the decimal place of the leading digit of its 95% interval half-width, and the bounds one more; a rate keeps at least two decimals (checked by `tests/test_numbers.py`). Every policy row other than version 1 is a post-hoc variant, not pre-registered.

## 1. Resolution limit (post-hoc descriptive)

| Condition | SNR at P(correct) = 0.90 (95% CI) | share of transformer energy at P(correct) = 0.90 (95% CI) |
|---|---|---|
| nominal (development grid, weeks 0–2) | 6 (5.2–7.3) | 0.16 (0.124–0.207) |
| held-out grid urban6, test weeks | 4.9 (4.21–5.65) | 0.08 (0.059–0.119) |
| development grid, test weeks | 6 (5.0–7.5) | 0.11 (0.080–0.165) |
| diversity d = 1.0 | 6 (5.0–8.1) | 0.27 (0.201–0.366) |
| midday events, PV × 2 | 9 (6.7–13.3) | 0.32 (0.245–0.444) |
| 10% random loss of readings | 8 (7.0–9.1) | 0.28 (0.219–0.351) |
| transformer-meter gain error sd 2% | 8 (6.3–9.4) | 0.21 (0.166–0.290) |
| load-shaped unmetered energy 5 kW | 25 (15.3–45.7) | 0.43 (0.302–0.683) |
| outage and comms failure at the same time | 13 (9.5–17.6) | 0.6 (0.33–1.07) |
| load-shaped unmetered energy 10 kW | 67 (33.4–325.2) | 1.0 (0.56–1.95) |

The SNR axis (expected silent energy divided by its predictive sd) is the most consistent across conditions: sd of log10 boundary 0.14 (share 0.20, kWh 0.44); held-out/dev ratio 0.81 (share 0.72).

**Scope of this limit.** It is fitted on labelled simulated events: outages and communication failures of whole branches, feeders and single connections in the episode mix. It does not describe the 1–2-meter silent groups created by random data loss. There, false outage verdicts arise at high apparent SNR (median 5.7 for single meters, development grid) as rare deep lower-tail residuals, multiplied by thousands of groups a year (§9).

## 2. Comparison at the version 1 safety limits (development validation weeks, every setting)

| Method | Highest coverage meeting all limits |
|---|---|
| likelihood-ratio test with abstention (primary, version 1) | 0.663 |
| likelihood-ratio test without abstention | cannot meet the limits |
| visible-share test | cannot meet the limits |
| two-sided z-test | 0.602 |
| naive share baseline | cannot meet the limits |
| step baseline | cannot meet the limits |
| count baseline | cannot meet the limits |
| structure baseline | cannot meet the limits |
| Isolation Forest (added after the held-out test) | cannot meet the limits |

**Why coverage is below 1 for methods without an abstention band.** The likelihood-ratio test without abstention, the visible-share test and the two-sided z-test answer UNCERTAIN when the expected energy of the silent group is below the minimum-energy threshold chosen for them on development validation weeks (`min_expected_kwh` in `results/detector_params.json`; rule at `shahid/detect.py:126`). The two-sided z-test also abstains when both or neither hypothesis fits (`shahid/detect.py:138`). The naive share baseline has its own minimum-energy rule (`shahid/baselines.py:64`), and the structure baseline abstains when the silent set is both a concentrator group and an electrical zone (`shahid/baselines.py:42`). The count and step baselines and the Isolation Forest never abstain.

Held-out paired coverage differences (cluster bootstrap): likelihood-ratio test with abstention − two-sided z-test 0.09 (0.049–0.131); likelihood-ratio test with abstention − visible-share test 0.00 (-0.042–0.047).

Isolation Forest cause attribution: AUC 0.41 (0.341–0.484) on development validation weeks (week 2), seeds 101-103, matched labelled episodes; direction: score = -IsolationForest.score_samples (higher = more anomalous), positive class = OUTAGE. The interval excludes 0.5 but lies below it: no evidence of cause attribution.

## 6. Policy components, separated (post-hoc variants, not pre-registered)

**Implementation status.** The meter-count gate and the comms re-check below are evaluated in study code (`shahid/cp12.py`, `shahid/p2eval.py`). Neither is executed by `explain.escalate`; `configs/escalation.yaml` states the R3 re-check only as action text, and the gate is not in it.

Registered outcome of the policy selection: infeasible: recommend version 1 alone. The meter-count gate (groups of fewer than 3 meters held in WATCH for 1 h) was selected under a declared deviation (docs/eval_protocol.md), and is not re-chosen. The comms re-check timeout is shown as a curve, not chosen. One matching rule (registered set overlap, docs/eval_protocol.md) is used everywhere. Human items are split into three types and never merged: uncertain (including WATCH timeouts), outage verdict awaiting approval, communication verdict unconfirmed.

### 6.5 Comms re-check: cost and benefit

**These results depend on the simulated duration of communication failures and on assumption A-COMMS (meters store readings and resend them when the link returns).** Simulated communication failures last: standard episode mix, development grid: median 2.50 h (10–90%: 1.25–3.75 h, range 1–4 h); whole-feeder events, held-out grid: median 2.50 h (10–90%: 1.25–4.00 h, range 1–4 h); untouched rural grid, test weeks: median 2.75 h (10–90%: 1.25–3.75 h, range 1–4 h). No simulated failure lasts longer than 4 h, so an 8 h re-check never escalates a genuine one in this simulation; that is a property of the simulator, not evidence for 8 h.

Whole-feeder outages reported as "never detected" under the combined variant (gate + re-check) in the earlier policy selection are not a matching artefact. That earlier column merged three outcomes. Under the registered match: whole-feeder events, development grid: watch closed no verdict 16, never detected 2 of 350 outages; whole-feeder events, held-out grid: watch closed no verdict 17, never detected 2 of 350 outages. Every "closed, no verdict" case is a whole feeder of 1–3 meters (simulated feeders can be that small). The gate holds it in WATCH, power returns within the 1 h WATCH timeout without the onset reading ever arriving, and the group is closed without a verdict and without a human. The genuinely undetected ones (no silent group formed) are missed by version 1 as well.

## 9. Why tiny groups produce confident false outage verdicts

Standardised residual z = (R − M)/sd_C at the decision time; nominal 90% interval |z| < 2.13 (Student-t, 4 df, the detector's own model).

Single meters, fault-free development year, validation weeks: of 526277 meter-intervals with an expectation of at least 0.05 kWh, a share of 0.0022 had an actual reading of at most 0.005 kWh; the detector's model implies 0.0510.

**Verdict on the hypothesis "predictive uncertainty is understated for very small groups": refuted for single meters, partly supported for two-meter groups.**

- Single meters: the 90% interval holds more than 90% of residuals, the deep lower tail is lighter than the model's, and near-zero readings are rarer than the model implies.
- Two-meter groups: the lower tail at the 90% bound is heavier than nominal.
- The false verdicts are deep-tail residuals that occur at roughly the rate the model itself allows. They add up to about 30 per transformer-year because random loss creates thousands of 1–2-meter silent groups a year and the decision uses a 50/50 prior. This is a base-rate problem, not a variance problem (`docs/process/phase2_candidates.md`).

## Do NOT report

- Accuracy-when-deciding without coverage; labelled-episode precision as field precision.
- A single headline rate without the range of §0.
- Bin-edge boundaries ("16%", "32%"); the balanced figure of the first threshold selection; the stuck-meter perfect score; smoke-test verdicts; dev-grid test weeks as held-out data.
- The combined variant (gate + re-check) as one policy: report its components separately (§6).
- "Robust", "generalises", "real-time", "deployed", "AI", "machine learning", "novel"; any Tunisian or STEG data or infrastructure claim.
- Earlier design figures listed as RETRACTED in the ledger.
